result.summary: Batches block file pruning into a single pass over the block index instead of iterating the entire index once per pruned file. A new method replaces `PruneOneBlockFile` by taking a set of file numbers and checking them against a bitfield during a single traversal of `m_block_index`.
result.problem: When enabling pruning on an existing unpruned node or manually pruning many files at once, the node iterated through every block in `m_block_index` separately for each file being pruned. On a full chain with thousands of block files, this O(M * N) operation performs billions of iterations and holds `cs_main` for tens of seconds to ten minutes, completely freezing node startup.
evidence: Author benchmarks with ~972k blocks and 5,770 files pruned demonstrate a drop from 75.1s to 14.7ms on x86_64 and 606.0s to 26.3ms on Raspberry Pi 5 while holding `cs_main` (PR description).
result.card: Batch block file pruning into a single pass over `m_block_index` instead of running one full index traversal per pruned file. When switching a full node to pruned mode or pruning large ranges, the previous O(M * N) algorithm froze the node while holding `cs_main` for up to 10 minutes on lower-end hardware like a Raspberry Pi 5. Benchmarks report reducing pruning time from 606s down to 26ms on ARM64 and 75s down to 15ms on x86_64.

risk.why: A bug in updating block index records during pruning could mark block data as pruned incorrectly or corrupt block index persistence to disk.
